It is tagging plain place-name layers as shields and skipping real shield layers. Is the heuristic sound, and what should it key off instead?","## TL;DR

* **`text‑anchor` and `symbol‑placement` are not reliable “shield” flags** – they are either omitted (meaning the defaults *center* / *point*) or they are set on *any* point‑symbol layer (place‑names, POIs, custom icons, etc.).
* The **real, spec‑defined signal that a symbol is a shield** is the **`icon‑text‑fit` layout property** (value `""both""`, `""width""` or `""height""`).

* In practice you’ll also want to look at the **`icon‑image` expression** (does it contain a `{ref}`‑related token such as `{ref_length}` or `{network}_{ref_length}`?) and, if you have access to the sprite JSON, whether the referenced image is **stretchable** (`stretchX`/`stretchY` + `content`).
Below is a short “cheat‑sheet” of why the old heuristic fails, what the spec says, and a concrete implementation you can drop into a style‑audit script.
## 1. Why the current heuristic is broken

column4: What actually happens in most styles

column3: `text-anchor` defaults to `""center""` when omitted. It is **not** a “shield‑only” property; it is used on *every* point‑symbol that has a text field (place‑names, POI labels, etc.).
column4: Most point‑symbol layers **don’t set** `text-anchor` explicitly, so the test is true for *all* of them.

column3: `symbol-placement` defaults to `""point""` for symbol layers that have an `icon-image`. It is the *default* for **any** point‑symbol, shield or not.
column4: Again, the majority of point‑symbol layers satisfy this condition.

column3: The conjunction therefore matches **any** point‑symbol layer that has a text field (or even none, because `text-anchor` is irrelevant when there is no text).
column4: Your script ends up flagging *every* place‑name / POI layer as a shield and missing the few real shield layers that happen to set `icon-text-fit` (or that rely on the default `icon-text-fit: none`).

column1: **Bottom line:** The two properties you are testing are *defaults*, not *opt‑ins*. They cannot be used to differentiate shields from ordinary point symbols.
## 2. What *is* a shield, according to the style spec
1. **Shows an icon (the badge) that is sized to fit the text** that sits on top of it.
*The spec‑defined way to request that behaviour is `icon-text-fit`* (values `""both""`, `""width""` or `""height""`). The default is `""none""`.
2. **Usually has a text field** (`text-field`) that contains the road reference (`{ref}`, `{ref_length}`, `{network}` etc.).
The text is rendered **inside** the badge, so the badge must be stretchable.
3. **References a stretchable sprite image** (or a runtime image with the same metadata). In the sprite JSON the image entry contains:
* a `content` rectangle that defines the “non‑stretchable core”, and
* optionally `textFitWidth` / `textFitHeight` (these are the same thing the style author could set via `icon-text-fit`).
If any of the above is missing, the layer will **not** behave like a shield.
> `""none""` (default) – no scaling. `""both""` – scale the icon to fit the text width **and** height.
* **`icon-image`** – the ID of the sprite image. When the image is a shield it is usually built with stretch metadata (see the sprite JSON spec).
* **`text-field`** – often an expression that pulls `{ref}` or `{network}` from the feature properties.
